BIOS 707 Checkpoint 2: building and comparing models on set-a¶

Predict in-hospital mortality from the first 48 hours of each ICU stay using regularized logistic regression, restricted cubic spline logistic regression, and a random forest. SAPS-I and SOFA are evaluated separately as risk scores. Only set-a is used; external evaluation belongs to Checkpoint 3.

AI-use statement and reflection¶

ChatGPT/Codex assisted with restructuring the notebook, debugging Python code, reviewing the modeling workflow against the instructor's requirements, and running reproducibility checks. The assistance included code generation and revision, not just language editing.

Advantages. AI helped consolidate repeated cleaning and model-training steps into one coherent workflow and automate repetitive checks. It also helped identify inconsistent MAP cleaning, an undefined variable in prediction saving, and differences between pooled OOF AUROC and mean fold AUROC. Shared CV folds, training-fold preprocessing, and checks of saved predictions made the revised analysis easier to reproduce and inspect.

Disadvantages. AI-generated code required execution and methodological verification. For example, an early AI-assisted revision introduced a string formatting error that interrupted notebook execution; it was corrected before the successful fresh-kernel run. Plausible implementations also needed checking against the assignment, including whether ordinary cubic splines satisfied the restricted cubic spline requirement. AI assistance did not independently validate the clinical cleaning thresholds or establish that a small AUROC difference was meaningful. These experiences show why generated code and interpretations should be checked against the instructor's requirements, source data, documentation, and actual execution results rather than accepted at face value. The submission author remains responsible for reviewing the final code, clinical assumptions, and interpretation.

2.1 The modeling table¶

The starting table is the wide table from Checkpoint 1. There is one row per ICU stay. Outcomes are joined from Data/Outcomes-a.txt by RecordID with a one-to-one constraint. All measurement summaries are rebuilt from raw set-a records to enforce the 0–48-hour window and consistent cleaning. This replaces the summary values in memory without changing Checkpoint 1 files.

Checkpoint 1's missing -1 codes for Gender, Height, and Weight and height range of 100–250 cm are carried forward. Zero height/weight is additionally treated as missing. The existing provisional temperature range of 25–45 °C and MAP lower bound of 30 mmHg are retained. These are analysis assumptions, not validated physiological boundaries, and may exclude extreme true values. No further screening thresholds are applied.

In [2]:
wide = pd.read_csv(ROOT / 'output' / 'set-a_wide.csv')
outcomes = pd.read_csv(DATA / 'Outcomes-a.txt',
                       usecols=['RecordID', 'In-hospital_death', 'SAPS-I', 'SOFA'])
base = wide.drop(columns=['In-hospital_death', 'SAPS-I', 'SOFA',
                          'Length_of_stay', 'Survival'], errors='ignore')
model_df = base.merge(outcomes, on='RecordID', how='left',
                      validate='one_to_one', sort=False)
ids = model_df.RecordID.to_numpy()
y = model_df['In-hospital_death'].reset_index(drop=True)
benchmarks = model_df[['SAPS-I', 'SOFA']].replace(-1, np.nan).reset_index(drop=True)

raw_files = sorted((DATA / 'set-a').glob('*.txt'))
records, record_headers = [], []
for path in raw_files:
    patient = pd.read_csv(path)
    recorded_id = patient.loc[patient.Parameter.eq('RecordID'), 'Value']
    record_headers.append((int(path.stem), recorded_id.tolist()))
    patient = patient.loc[~patient.Parameter.eq('RecordID')].copy()
    patient['RecordID'] = int(path.stem)
    records.append(patient)
raw = pd.concat(records, ignore_index=True)
parts = raw.Time.str.split(':', expand=True).astype(int)
raw['Minutes'] = parts[0]*60 + parts[1]
raw['Value'] = pd.to_numeric(raw.Value, errors='raise')
outside_window = int((~raw.Minutes.between(0, 2880)).sum())
clean = raw.loc[raw.Minutes.between(0, 2880)].copy()
audit = []
rules = [
    ('-1 demographic codes', clean.Parameter.isin(['Gender','Height','Weight']) & clean.Value.eq(-1)),
    ('Zero height/weight', clean.Parameter.isin(['Height','Weight']) & clean.Value.eq(0)),
    ('Height outside 100–250 cm', clean.Parameter.eq('Height') & ~clean.Value.between(100,250)),
    ('Temperature outside 25–45 C', clean.Parameter.eq('Temp') & ~clean.Value.between(25,45)),
    ('MAP below 30 mmHg', clean.Parameter.eq('MAP') & clean.Value.lt(30)),
]
for label, mask in rules:
    affected = mask & clean.Value.notna()
    audit.append({'Rule': label, 'Measurements removed': int(affected.sum()),
                  'Stays affected': clean.loc[affected, 'RecordID'].nunique()})
    clean.loc[affected, 'Value'] = np.nan
# Stable order preserves source ordering for simultaneous measurements.
clean = clean.sort_values(['RecordID','Minutes'], kind='stable')
summaries = clean.groupby(['RecordID','Parameter']).Value.agg(
    ['count','first','last','min','max','mean']).unstack('Parameter')
summaries.columns = [f'{parameter}_{stat}' for stat, parameter in summaries.columns]
rebuilt = summaries.reindex(ids).reset_index(drop=True)
rebuilt_columns = set(rebuilt.columns)
for col in rebuilt.columns:
    model_df[col] = rebuilt[col].to_numpy()
cleaning_audit = pd.DataFrame(audit)
display(cleaning_audit)
check = pd.DataFrame({
    'Check': ['Measurements outside 0–48 h', '141449 temperature before cleaning',
              '141449 valid temperature', 'Stays without valid MAP',
              'Missing SAPS-I', 'Missing SOFA'],
    'Observed': [outside_window,
        int((raw.RecordID.eq(141449) & raw.Parameter.eq('Temp') & raw.Minutes.between(0,2880)).sum()),
        int(model_df.loc[model_df.RecordID.eq(141449),'Temp_count'].iloc[0]),
        int(model_df.MAP_count.fillna(0).eq(0).sum()),
        int(benchmarks['SAPS-I'].isna().sum()), int(benchmarks.SOFA.isna().sum())],
    'Historical reference': [0,65,39,1211,190,144]})
del records, raw, clean, summaries, rebuilt

2.2 Predictors¶

Clinical trajectories are represented by first/last, minimum/maximum, and mean values. Counts and measured indicators describe monitoring intensity and missingness, which may reflect clinician concern and care practices.

Age, Gender, Height, and ICUType retain their first valid value only; redundant summaries and counts of these baseline fields are dropped. Repeated weight measurements remain summarized. Gender and ICUType are categorical, including in the random forest. No variable is dropped because it is rarely measured; sparse laboratory variables are retained with training-fold imputation and measurement-pattern features. Predictor counts below refer to raw columns, before one-hot encoding or spline expansion.

In [3]:
excluded = ['RecordID','In-hospital_death','SAPS-I','SOFA','Length_of_stay','Survival']
X = model_df.drop(columns=excluded, errors='ignore').copy()
static = ['Age','Gender','Height','ICUType']
redundant = [f'{v}_{s}' for v in static for s in ['count','last','min','max','mean']]
X = X.drop(columns=redundant)
counts = [c for c in X if c.endswith('_count')]
for col in counts:
    X[col] = X[col].fillna(0)
    X[col.removesuffix('_count') + '_measured'] = X[col].gt(0).astype(int)
categorical = ['Gender_first','ICUType_first']
numeric = [c for c in X if c not in categorical]
X_spline = X[spline_cols + linear_cols].copy()
rationales = {
    'first': 'Initial available condition; baseline demographics when static.',
    'last': 'Most recent condition within the observation window.',
    'min': 'Lowest recorded value may reflect physiological deterioration.',
    'max': 'Highest recorded value may reflect physiological stress.',
    'mean': 'Typical level over the observation window.',
    'count': 'Intensity of clinical monitoring using valid measurements.',
    'measured': 'Whether at least one valid measurement was available.'}
inventory = pd.DataFrame([{'Predictor': c, 'Group': c.rsplit('_',1)[1],
    'Type': 'categorical' if c in categorical else 'numeric',
    'Clinical rationale': rationales[c.rsplit('_',1)[1]],
    'Missing (%)': 100*X[c].isna().mean()} for c in X])
dropped = pd.DataFrame({'Column': redundant + excluded,
    'Reason': ['Redundant baseline-field summary']*len(redundant) +
              ['Identifier','Outcome','Benchmark only','Benchmark only',
               'Post-observation information','Post-observation information']})
display(inventory.groupby('Group', sort=False).agg(
    Predictors=('Predictor','size'), Rationale=('Clinical rationale','first')))
print(f'Total predictors: {X.shape[1]} ({len(numeric)} numerical, {len(categorical)} categorical)')
# The complete inventory and dropped-column list are included in the report.
display(inventory[['Predictor','Group','Type','Clinical rationale','Missing (%)']].style.hide(axis='index'))
display(dropped)

2.3 Cross-validation design¶

Five stratified outer folds (seed 42) are created once and reused for all three models and both benchmarks. One row per stay makes grouping unnecessary. Three stratified inner folds (seed 42) tune each configuration using only the outer training portion. Imputation, scaling, encoding, and spline knot placement are fitted within the pipelines in each training fold. Deterministic cleaning rules are fixed before CV; no outcome-based feature selection is performed.

Mean outer-fold AUROC estimates each tuning procedure. Selecting the final model family after inspecting those results can still be optimistic. These are development results, not an independent external evaluation.

Data and CV validation¶

The following section checks patient IDs, outcome alignment, feature integrity, measurement-count consistency, and fold membership once before any model fitting. The one-to-one merge constraint also guards data ingestion. Output round-trip checks later test serialization rather than repeating these data checks.

In [4]:

inner_cv = StratifiedKFold(n_splits=3, shuffle=True, random_state=SEED)

def preprocessing(scale=True):
    steps = [('imputer', SimpleImputer(strategy='median', keep_empty_features=True))]
    if scale:
        steps.append(('scaler', StandardScaler()))
    return ColumnTransformer([
        ('numeric', Pipeline(steps), numeric),
        ('categorical', Pipeline([
            ('imputer', SimpleImputer(strategy='most_frequent', keep_empty_features=True)),
            ('encoder', OneHotEncoder(drop='first', handle_unknown='ignore',
                                      sparse_output=False))]), categorical)])

fold_results, oof, specifications, full_searches = {}, {}, {}, {}
def evaluate(name, estimator, grid, frame):
    prediction = np.full(len(y), np.nan)
    rows = []
    for fold, (train, valid) in enumerate(splits, 1):
        search = GridSearchCV(clone(estimator), grid, scoring='roc_auc', cv=inner_cv,
                              n_jobs=N_JOBS, refit=True, error_score='raise')
        with joblib.parallel_backend('threading', n_jobs=N_JOBS):
            search.fit(frame.iloc[train], y.iloc[train])
        prediction[valid] = search.predict_proba(frame.iloc[valid])[:,1]
        score = roc_auc_score(y.iloc[valid], prediction[valid])
        rows.append({'Fold':fold, 'AUROC':score, 'n':len(valid),
                     'Deaths':int(y.iloc[valid].sum()),
                     'Best parameters': json.dumps(search.best_params_)})
        print(f'{name}: fold {fold}/5 AUROC={score:.4f}', flush=True)
    assert np.isfinite(prediction).all() and ((prediction>=0)&(prediction<=1)).all()
    fold_results[name], oof[name] = pd.DataFrame(rows), prediction
    specifications[name] = (estimator, grid, frame)
    display(fold_results[name])

def full_fit(name):
    """One full-set-a fit per model, reused for final selection and diagnostics."""
    if name not in full_searches:
        estimator, grid, frame = specifications[name]
        search = GridSearchCV(clone(estimator), grid, scoring='roc_auc', cv=inner_cv,
                              n_jobs=N_JOBS, error_score='raise', refit=True)
        with joblib.parallel_backend('threading', n_jobs=N_JOBS):
            search.fit(frame, y)
        full_searches[name] = search
        print(name, 'full-set-a configuration:', search.best_params_)
    return full_searches[name].best_estimator_

2.4 Model 1: Ridge logistic regression¶

Ridge (L2) regularization shrinks correlated trajectory summaries without discarding predictors. The inner-CV grid is C = 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100; smaller C means stronger regularization. Ridge does not perform sparse feature selection, so a selected-variable stability analysis is not applicable.

In [5]:
ridge = Pipeline([('preprocessor', preprocessing()),
                  ('model', LogisticRegression(l1_ratio=0.0, solver='lbfgs', max_iter=5000,
                                                random_state=SEED))])
c_grid = {'model__C':[0.01,0.1,1,10,100]}
evaluate('Ridge Logistic', ridge, c_grid, X)

2.5 Model 2: restricted cubic spline logistic regression¶

Fourteen clinical predictors are prespecified for interpretability: age, hemodynamics, temperature, renal function, neurological status, hematology, electrolytes, glucose, and weight. Age, mean HR, and mean temperature receive restricted cubic splines; the other 11 enter linearly. Four knots are placed at training-fold quantiles 0.05, 0.35, 0.65, 0.95 after training-fold imputation. All three nonlinear functions have linear tails beyond the boundary knots.

The basis uses SciPy's natural cubic interpolation and explicit tangent-line extension: natural boundary conditions alone do not guarantee linear extrapolation (SciPy documentation). The custom transformer in scripts/cp2_support.py learns no validation data. This implementation satisfies the restricted cubic spline specification. C uses the same five-value inner-CV grid.

In [6]:
spline_pre = ColumnTransformer([
    ('spline', Pipeline([
        ('imputer', SimpleImputer(strategy='median', keep_empty_features=True)),
        ('basis', RestrictedCubicSpline()), ('scaler', StandardScaler())]), spline_cols),
    ('linear', Pipeline([
        ('imputer', SimpleImputer(strategy='median', keep_empty_features=True)),
        ('scaler', StandardScaler())]), linear_cols)])
spline = Pipeline([('preprocessor', spline_pre),
                   ('model', LogisticRegression(solver='lbfgs', max_iter=5000,
                                                 random_state=SEED))])
evaluate('Spline Logistic', spline, c_grid, X_spline)

2.6 Model 3: random forest¶

The forest captures nonlinear relationships and interactions across the full feature table. Numeric missing values use training-fold median imputation; categorical values use training-fold mode imputation and one-hot encoding. Explicit measurement counts and indicators are shared with Ridge. No additional automatically generated imputation indicators are introduced.

The forest has 200 trees and seed 42. Inner CV evaluates max_depth in {10,20}, min_samples_leaf in {2,5}, and max_features='sqrt'. No early stopping is used.

In [7]:

forest_grid = {'model__max_depth':[10,20], 'model__min_samples_leaf':[2,5],
               'model__max_features':['sqrt']}
evaluate('Random Forest', forest, forest_grid, X)

2.7 Comparison and choice of final model¶

SAPS-I and SOFA are evaluated alone, with higher scores interpreted as greater risk. -1 is missing. The primary benchmark analysis uses observed scores within the same outer folds, without fitting or imputing the scores. Fold sample sizes and death counts are reported. Missing scores remain NaN in the OOF file.

Because available-score subsets differ from the full model cohort, paired within-fold comparisons below also evaluate all three models on each benchmark's observed-score subset. The ROC legend uses pooled OOF AUROC, whereas the comparison table reports mean fold AUROC and sample SD; these are distinct summaries.

In [8]:
for name in ['SAPS-I','SOFA']:
    scores = benchmarks[name].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    rows = []
    for fold, (_, valid) in enumerate(splits,1):
        observed = valid[np.isfinite(scores[valid])]
        assert y.iloc[observed].nunique()==2
        rows.append({'Fold':fold,'AUROC':roc_auc_score(y.iloc[observed],scores[observed]),
                     'n':len(observed),'Deaths':int(y.iloc[observed].sum()),
                     'Best parameters':'Not fitted'})
    fold_results[name], oof[name] = pd.DataFrame(rows), scores

    comparison.loc[name,'Evaluated n'] = np.isfinite(oof[name]).sum()

    Mean_difference=('Difference','mean'),SD_difference=('Difference','std'))

# Practical simplicity preference: retain Ridge when its mean AUROC is
# within 0.01 of the best method. This is a practical rule, not a significance test.

# This is a development-CV model choice; external test data remain untouched.
final_model = full_fit(selected)

    'not evidence of equivalence or statistical significance.']

        'than one SD of the paired fold differences. This is a descriptive '

Results and selection¶

Final model: Ridge Logistic. Highest mean-AUROC model: Random Forest. Ridge gap: 0.0024. Ridge is preferred within that margin for simplicity and coefficient-based interpretability. The 0.01 preference is a practical choice, not evidence of equivalence or statistical significance.

On the SAPS-I-available cohort, Random Forest exceeds SAPS-I by 0.1965 mean fold AUROC (fold-difference SD 0.0372). The mean improvement is larger than one SD of the paired fold differences. This is a descriptive comparison; five dependent CV folds do not supply an independent significance test.

On the SOFA-available cohort, Random Forest exceeds SOFA by 0.2250 mean fold AUROC (fold-difference SD 0.0356). The mean improvement is larger than one SD of the paired fold differences. This is a descriptive comparison; five dependent CV folds do not supply an independent significance test.

Required full-data diagnostic plots¶

Outer-CV predictions estimate performance and are never replaced by full-data predictions. The selected final model is tuned and refitted on all set-a only after model comparison. Ridge and spline full-data fits are also needed for the instructor's coefficient and partial-effect plots, regardless of which model is selected. Each full-data fit is cached and reused; none repeats outer CV.

The coefficient figure shows every encoded predictor on a common SD scale. Coefficients are multiplied by their encoded predictor SD in the full-set-a refit, including one-hot contrasts. This visualization does not change model fitting. Orange bars denote categorical contrasts. Constant predictors have zero standardized coefficients; reference levels and original contrast coefficients are reported separately. Associations are not causal effects.

In [9]:
ridge_final = full_fit('Ridge Logistic')
pre = ridge_final.named_steps['preprocessor']
coef = pd.DataFrame({'Predictor':pre.get_feature_names_out(),
                     'Coefficient':ridge_final.named_steps['model'].coef_[0]})
coef['Scale'] = np.where(coef.Predictor.str.startswith('numeric__'),
                         'Per training-set SD', 'Category vs reference')
# Post-fit visualization only: put every encoded predictor on a common SD scale.
# Numerical pipeline outputs have SD=1 except constant features. One-hot contrasts
# are multiplied by their empirical SD; this does not change model fitting.
encoded_sd = np.std(pre.transform(X), axis=0, ddof=0)
coef['Encoded predictor SD'] = encoded_sd
coef['Standardized coefficient'] = coef.Coefficient * encoded_sd
ordered = coef.sort_values('Standardized coefficient').reset_index(drop=True)
chunks = np.array_split(np.arange(len(ordered)), 4)
fig_all, axes_all = plt.subplots(1, 4, figsize=(24, 19), sharex=True)
limit = max(ordered['Standardized coefficient'].abs().max() * 1.08, .01)
for panel, (ax, positions) in enumerate(zip(axes_all, chunks), 1):
    section = ordered.iloc[positions]
    labels = section.Predictor.str.replace('numeric__', '', regex=False).str.replace('categorical__', '', regex=False)
    colors = np.where(section.Scale.eq('Category vs reference'), '#d97706', '#2878b5')
    ax.barh(labels, section['Standardized coefficient'], color=colors)
    ax.axvline(0, color='gray', lw=.8)
    ax.set(xlim=(-limit, limit), xlabel='Log-odds coefficient per 1 SD',
           title=f'All Ridge coefficients: panel {panel}/4')
    ax.tick_params(axis='y', labelsize=8)
fig_all.suptitle('Full-set-a Ridge: all encoded coefficients on a common SD scale', fontsize=16)
fig_all.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0, 1, .98))
fig_all.savefig(RUN/'ridge_coefficients_all.png', dpi=160)

# Stay-level percentile bootstrap; the selected C is fixed, preprocessing refits.
reference = X_spline.median().to_dict()
effect_data = {}
for feature in spline_cols:
    grid = np.linspace(X_spline[feature].quantile(.01), X_spline[feature].quantile(.99), 100)
    plot_frame = pd.DataFrame([reference]*len(grid))[X_spline.columns]
    reference_frame = plot_frame.copy()
    plot_frame[feature] = grid
    effect_data[feature] = {'grid':grid, 'plot':plot_frame, 'ref':reference_frame, 'boot':[]}
rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)
for b in range(N_BOOTSTRAP):
    sample = rng.choice(len(y), len(y), replace=True)
    boot = clone(spline_final).fit(X_spline.iloc[sample], y.iloc[sample])
    for info in effect_data.values():
        info['boot'].append(boot.decision_function(info['plot'])-boot.decision_function(info['ref']))
    if (b+1)%25 == 0:
        print(f'Bootstrap {b+1}/{N_BOOTSTRAP}', flush=True)

labels = {'Age_first':'Age (years)', 'HR_mean':'Mean HR (beats/min)', 'Temp_mean':'Mean temperature (C)'}
for ax, (feature,info) in zip(axes,effect_data.items()):
    effect = spline_final.decision_function(info['plot'])-spline_final.decision_function(info['ref'])
    lower, upper = np.percentile(info['boot'],[2.5,97.5],axis=0)
    ax.plot(info['grid'],effect,label='Fitted effect')
    ax.fill_between(info['grid'],lower,upper,alpha=.25,label='95% pointwise bootstrap band')
    ax.axhline(0,color='gray',ls='--'); ax.axvline(reference[feature],color='gray',ls=':')
    ax.set(xlabel=labels[feature],ylabel='Log-odds difference vs median',title=feature)
    ax.legend(fontsize=8)
    effect_rows.append(pd.DataFrame({'Predictor':feature,'Value':info['grid'],
        'Reference':reference[feature],'Log_odds_difference':effect,'Lower':lower,'Upper':upper}))
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(RUN/'spline_partial_effects.png',dpi=180); plt.show()
effects = pd.concat(effect_rows,ignore_index=True)
print('Reference values:', {c:round(reference[c],3) for c in spline_cols})

Age: The fitted association increases with age and becomes steeper at older ages, suggesting nonlinearity rather than a constant linear slope. Higher risk with advanced age is clinically plausible, but this is an adjusted association.

Heart rate: The curve has a shallow trough around 75–80 beats/min followed by a stronger increase at high mean HR. Its asymmetric U/J shape is consistent with tachycardia reflecting physiological stress; the low-HR association is uncertain because its band includes the reference effect.

Temperature: The curve is asymmetric and nonlinear, with higher fitted risk at lower temperatures, a trough near 37.4 C, and a small rise at higher temperatures. Low temperature can accompany severe illness; the high-temperature rise is uncertain because the band includes the reference effect.

Effects are log-odds differences from the predictor's median, holding the other predictors at their medians. Bands are pointwise percentile intervals from 100 stay-level bootstrap refits, conditional on the selected C. They do not include tuning uncertainty, are not simultaneous bands, and do not establish causality. These interpretations describe the observed set-a fit and are not formal tests of nonlinearity.

Save final results and verify serialization¶

Each model's OOF predictions were generated once in the shared outer-CV loop. All final tables, the selected fitted pipeline, and the single aligned OOF table are saved here. CSV and model reload checks verify that serialization preserves the results; they do not rerun cleaning, feature construction, or model CV.

Limitations and handoff to Checkpoint 3¶

The provisional cleaning boundaries may discard true extremes. Monitoring features can encode care practices and may transfer poorly. Benchmark score missingness can make the available-score cohorts selective, even with matched comparisons. The selected model family's development AUROC can be optimistic; external discrimination and calibration have not been evaluated here.

The saved pipeline expects the cleaned feature columns recorded in metadata, not raw patient files. Apply the same deterministic 0–48-hour feature construction before using it in Checkpoint 3. If the spline model is selected, retain scripts/cp2_support.py on the import path when loading its artifact. Set-b and set-c must remain untouched until Checkpoint 3. Calibration, decision curves, subgroups, and SHAP are outside the current checkpoint.
